findings.title: Channel funding draft silently drops the unspent part of the funding coin
findings.summary: buildFundingTx takes explicit input amounts but always emits exactly one output (the channel coin). It neither returns change nor checks that inputs cover outputs, and buildChannelOpening passes the whole funding coin. Opening a channel from a coin larger than localAmount + remoteAmount therefore produces a draft whose inputs exceed its outputs by the unspent remainder. tx-builder buildTransaction does not check conservation either, so nothing fails until a node rejects the unbalanced transaction.
findings.impact: Reachable from the RPC surface: omnia-host forwards fundingCoinId unchanged, so any wallet that does not pre-select an exactly-sized coin fails to open a channel with an opaque node rejection. No funds are lost (the node refuses the transaction) but the failure is late and misattributed.

repro.expected: The draft either pays the remainder back to the funding coin address (change output) or throws when sum(inputs) > totalValue.
repro.actual: The draft contains a single output. inputs sum 1500 while outputs sum 1000, and no layer rejects it. Recorded as a node:test TODO so it stays visible without failing the gate.
evidence: CANARY FINDING: an over-funded funding draft is neither changed nor rejected (TODO)
packages/omnia/src/channel.ts: buildChannelOpening passes fundingCoin.amount as the input
packages/tx-builder/src/build.ts: buildTransaction has no conservation check

fix.approach: Add a change output to the input coin address in buildFundingTx when sum(inputs) > totalValue, or reject the draft with a clear error. Do both at the right layers: omnia owns channel funding semantics, tx-builder should refuse to serialise an unbalanced transaction rather than deferring to the node.
constraints: Do not change the funding output state contract: STATE(100)=false, STATE(101)=0.
Do not change computeOmniaTxDigest / canonical byte semantics.
Do not mask this in the canary, in omnia-host, or with a coin pre-selection workaround.
Keep the single-input fast path byte-identical when the input equals totalValue.
acceptance: buildFundingTx returns a change output to the funding coin address when inputs exceed totalValue.
buildFundingTx (or buildChannelOpening) throws when inputs are less than totalValue.
tx-builder buildTransaction rejects a draft whose input sum is below its output sum.
Unit tests cover over-funded, exact, and under-funded inputs.
The canary test "over-funded funding draft is neither changed nor rejected" is un-TODOed and passes.

findings.title: Manifest proofs are not bound to the manifest they attest
findings.summary: verifyManifestProof verifies the manifest signature and the proof envelope independently and never compares them. A proof whose payload.manifestId names a different manifest, a proof of a different kind (attestation), and a proof issued by an unrelated key all verify as valid against any correctly signed manifest.
findings.impact: An attestation issued for one manifest can be presented as attestation for another (for example a later version with the same appId), and a non-manifest proof can be passed off as a manifest attestation. Verifiers that rely on the pairing will over-report assurance.

repro.expected: A proof for manifest A is rejected against manifest B, a non-manifest proof is rejected, and a foreign issuer is rejected.
repro.actual: All three return valid: true, because verifyManifestProof never reads proof.payload, proof.kind or the proof issuer relative to the manifest.
evidence: createManifestProof stores payload { manifestId } from the caller, and nothing compares it back
canary observed: proof for A vs manifest B -> valid; attestation proof vs manifest A -> valid; proof with unrelated manifestId -> valid; proof from a third-party issuer -> valid

fix.approach: Bind the pair explicitly: require proof.kind === 'manifest', require the proof issuer to be the manifest author address, and compare payload.manifestId with the identifier computed from the supplied manifest. Decide and document which identifier that is (content digest via computeManifestId is the strongest; appId is weaker and would still allow version substitution), then make createManifestProof derive it from the SignedManifest rather than trusting a caller string.
constraints: Do not change the manifest signing format or computeManifestId semantics.
Do not accept a wildcard or "any" manifestId to preserve callers.
Keep verifyManifest false-paths and reasons unchanged.
acceptance: verifyManifestProof rejects a proof issued for a different manifest (version substitution).
verifyManifestProof rejects a proof whose kind is not manifest.
verifyManifestProof rejects a proof whose issuer does not match the manifest author.
The honest proof/manifest pair still verifies.
The canary TODO test flips to a normal passing test.

findings.title: 41 publishable packages declare no test:integration gate
findings.summary: The maturity gate requires test:integration for RC packages, but these declare none and carry no reasoned notApplicable exemption. They are invisible to `verify-workspace --integration`.
findings.impact: A behavioural regression in any of these packages reaches a release with no integration evidence; the canary cannot cover them all on its own.

repro.expected: Every RC package either declares test:integration or a reasoned exemption.

where: the packages listed in this finding
fix.approach: Add a real test:integration per package (packed-consumer or invariant check), or record a reasoned notApplicable exemption in scripts/workspace-gates.config.json naming an owner.
constraints: Do not add notApplicable entries without an owner and a reason.
Do not add a script that always exits 0.
acceptance: node scripts/verify-workspace.mjs --integration reports no missing test:integration for RC packages.
Each new suite asserts behaviour, not just an import.

findings.title: Two unit suites exceed Jest's 5s default timeout under load
findings.source: canary core exercise: omnia-host prepare-submit-settle, lookup-node lease
findings.summary: The full unit suites fail on a loaded machine because individual tests inherit the 5,000 ms default. omnia-host prepareSettle/submitSettle takes ~15s end to end; lookup-node LEASE_RESERVE passes in 3s alone but exceeds 5s inside the 108s suite. Both pass when given 60s.
findings.impact: CI flakiness and false reds: the suites are green on a fast runner and red on a busy one, so a real regression and a slow machine look identical. It also blocks the canary from exercising these packages as part of a full run.

repro.actual: omnia-host: 1 failed / 125 passed (Exceeded timeout of 5000 ms). lookup-node: 1 failed / 70 passed. Both pass with --testTimeout=60000.
evidence: rerun with --testTimeout=60000: 1 passed / 125 skipped, and 1 passed / 70 skipped

fix.approach: Give the specific long tests an explicit timeout that reflects their work (settlement signing and a real lease round-trip), rather than raising the default for every test in the repo.
constraints: Do not set a repo-wide 60s default; it hides genuine hangs.
Do not skip or retry the tests.
acceptance: The full suites pass twice in a row on a loaded machine.
The timeout is scoped to the tests that need it, with a comment saying why.
